question: What is term used for perks that employers give to their employees above and beyond any financial compensation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fringe benefits.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fringe benefits:**

 
 
• The **extra perks provided to an employee above and beyond their stated pay in exchange for performing a particular function **are known as fringe benefits.
 
• These are the **perks that employers give to their employees above and beyond any financial compensation.**
 
• Certain universal perks are provided to all workers in an organisation, while others might only be available to executives.
 
• While some perks are intended to cover work-related expenses, others are intended to promote overall worker satisfaction.
 
• These **consist of below-market loans, employee discounts, employee stock options, health and life insurance, childcare reimbursement, cafeteria subsidies, tuition help, and personal use of a corporate vehicles.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Financial compensation:**

 
 
• **Encouraging someone with cash or other valuables in return for their services, labour, or to cover medical expenses related to an injury they have sustained** is known as financial compensation.
 
• **Main goal** of financial compensation is **to keep the ties between people who are trading goods and services intact.**
 
• **Wages, overtime pay, salaries, commissions, piece work rates, bonuses, and tips** are examples of common financial compensation.
 
 
 
• **Marginal Benefits:**
 
 
• The **utmost price a customer is prepared to pay for an extra good or service** is known as the marginal benefit.
 
• When a buyer purchases an additional good or service, they also gain additional enjoyment or usefulness.
 
• As a good or service is consumed more frequently, the consumer's marginal utility usually declines.
 
• **In the business sector, marginal revenue is a common term used to describe the producers' marginal advantage.**
